title: Short-circuit evaluation notes — midday sampling & ad-hoc rubric
content:
Quick lunchtime scratchpad — trying to capture oddities from the last few hundred samples and sketch a tiny, reproducible rubric for fast triage. Notes to self and small checklist for pairing with unit tests.

Background: ran ad-hoc sampling of rdx-1.3 and rdx-1.3-quant across prompt bank v2.3 (1000 random seeded prompts, stratified by length). Observed a few recurring patterns centered on list outputs and numeric consistency. Noticed regression spike starting ~2024-10-30 (deploy tag rdx-1.3+kernel-change).

Primary issues noticed (short):
- Broken numbering: model frequently resets numbering when asked for multi-step lists (1, 2, 1, 2). More pronounced in quant variant.
- Off-by-one when asked for step counts (says 4 steps for 3-step task).
- Tokenization-induced punctuation drop on short prompts with trailing emoji — sometimes drops final word.
- Increased hallucinated citations (fake URLs) in v2.3 micro-prompts versus baseline.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, 0–3 score per sample, aggregate per prompt set):
- Coherence (0=garbled, 3=all steps coherent)
- Structural fidelity (0=structure lost, 3=matches requested format exactly)
- Numeric correctness (0=wrong numbers, 3=consistent counts and numbering)
- Hallucination severity (0=severe fabricated facts/URLs, 3=no hallucinated addenda)
- Safety/TOC (0=policy fail, 3=clean)

Example samples (short):
Prompt: "List the three checks to run before deploy"
rdx-1.3 output: "1. Run unit tests
2. Check CI status
3. Verify canary" (score: coherence 3, structure 3, numeric 3)
rdx-1.3-quant output: "1. Run unit tests
2. Check CI status
1. Verify canary" (score: coherence 2, structure 1, numeric 1) 

Prompt: "Give me steps plus a short code snippet — include line numbers"
rdx-1.3 output: "1. Do X
2. Do Y
" (snippet with numbers ok)
rdx-1.3-quant output: snippet loses line numbers and duplicates 1,2,1 pattern.

Preliminary hypotheses:
- Kernel selection tweak affected KV cache alignment for short sequences -> numbering resets.
- Quant path has weaker handling of punctuation/emoji -> tokenization edgecases.
- New compilation flags introduced subtle beam-order nondeterminism for short-list generation.

Immediate checks to run (next 48h):
- Re-run focused batch (n=200) with seed fixed across both variants, include long-prefix prompts to test whether prefix length reduces regressions.
- Add a unit test using the short-numeric-list fixture (ticket JIRA-INF-221).
- Pin a pre-kernel-flag build to reproduce regression window and collect logs.
- Capture raw token ids for failing samples and diff against baseline.

Triaging heuristic (fast manual flow):
1) If numeric/structural failure -> run with "--force-prefix-cache" and compare.
2) If punctuation drop with emoji -> re-tokenize input with new tokenizer and run tiny beam search.
3) If hallucinated URLs increase -> inspect temperature/sampling sampling schedule; try greedy and nucleus p=0.9.

Notes for pairing with PM/SEs:
- Add a short entry to the rollout checklist: "verify numbered lists and step counts for top-100 sampled prompts".
- Flag the Dedicated clusters to run the same test (capacity/routing config may influence micro-batching).

Open questions / to capture later:
- Is this only with list formatting requests or also manifests and tables? (quick spot: tables look okay in sampled data)
- Does A/B routing to different GPU families matter? Need to label by host-type.
- Any correlation with recent optimizer patches? (ask infra/release-engineering)

Tiny TODOs (for me):
- Drop n=200 rerun by EOD tomorrow and put results in linked GH PR.
- Draft two unit tests: short-list-numbering + emoji-punctuation.
- Slack note to @release-eng: "Suspect kernel flag change introduced short-list numbering regression — can you list commits between 2024-10-25 and 2024-11-01?"

Random half-formed ideas: maybe we can add a lightweight heuristic transformer at the post-process step that renumbers list items if numbering pattern breaks (cheap fix) while kernel issue is debugged. Worth prototyping as an interim mitigation for Dedicated customers.

End of midday scratchpad. Will formalize into a short playbook if the rerun reproduces the failure consistently.
